# Videos from HTML — plan and research

Plan and notes for the third AI piece: how the four narrated explainers on
this site were made — HTML compositions rendered by HyperFrames, narration
from Kokoro — with the numbers from re-running the pipeline. Started
2026-09-13.

Audience: someone who writes, has an article they want a short video of, and
would rather not learn a video editor or pay a service. The four videos here
were all made that way, by an agent, in a day each.

## What was verified, and how

| Claim | Checked against |
|---|---|
| What HyperFrames is, how it renders, its rules | The repository README, the concepts / audio / export / rules docs pages, `render --help`, read in full |
| What Kokoro is, its size, licence, voices, price for scale | The repository README and the Kokoro-82M model card |
| How the four videos are built | The four projects in `video/` — READMEs, `index.html`, every composition |
| What `--low-memory-mode` does | The CLI's own `--help` text — which differs from what the project README says it does; see below |
| The pipeline's speed on a laptop | Re-run here: `check`, `tts`, `render` — [`notes/run.md`](/ai/research/local-agent/run.md) |

**A correction the research turned up.** The finance video's README says
`--low-memory-mode` "encodes as it captures" and avoids 25 GB of PNGs. The
CLI documents the flag as a *safe profile*: one worker, screenshot capture,
no worker calibration, auto-enabled on machines with 8 GB or less. The disk
overrun that session hit was real; the flag's documented purpose is memory,
and the documented answer to a small temp partition is `--frames-cache-dir`.
The article says both.

Not run: the Studio preview (a browser UI I cannot see this session), the
`publish` command (uploads the project), and Kokoro's reference `pip install
kokoro` path (the projects use `kokoro-onnx`).

## Decisions

1. **The four videos are the worked example.** They exist, they shipped,
   their sources are in the repository; nothing is built for the article.
2. **Measure the pipeline again rather than quote the READMEs.** Check,
   synthesis, render — wall time, output size, and whether a re-render is
   byte-identical to the shipped file.
3. **Say what the flag does, not what it felt like it did.** The
   `--low-memory-mode` correction above.
4. **The cold-seek rules get a section.** They are the non-obvious part of
   "HTML in, video out" — why a preview can look right and a render wrong —
   and they are why the linter exists.
5. **Kokoro's respelling trick is worth a paragraph.** "College-ika" is the
   kind of thing every narrated project hits.

## Traps hit

- The docs are MDX with React components inline; fetching `.md` returns
  the source, so the prose had to be filtered out of the code.
- `render --help` is where the flag's real meaning lives; the docs site's
  prose does not repeat it.
